rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads “and He provides whomever He wills” as an explanatory gloss on the preceding grants of sovereignty, honor, and related acts; the conjunction explicates a specific ruling through a broader one.
rows.anchor: فالعطف عطف تفسير فيكون من قبيل بيان الخاص من الحكم بما هو أعم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In Your hand is good” likewise explains the preceding acts; God directs creation through these acts because He provides whomever He wills without account.
rows.anchor: كما أن قوله { بيدك الخير } بالنسبة إلى ما سبقه من هذا القبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾānic usage of rizq retains a sense of gift: a king’s assigned allowance for a soldier was called rizqa, initially for food.
rows.anchor: فيه شوبا من معنى العطاء كرزق الملك الجندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq once meant food alone; 2:233 distinguishes the mother’s provision from clothing, showing that clothing was not included in the original restricted sense.
rows.anchor: فلم يعد الكسوة رزقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term broadened from nourishment to anything beneficial that reaches a being, including wealth, standing, kin, supporters, beauty, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: ثم عمم فسمى كل ما يصل إلى الشيء مما ينتفع به رزقا وإن لم يكن غذاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 11:88, Shuʿayb’s “good provision” refers to prophethood and knowledge, illustrating the broader Qurʾānic sense of rizq.
rows.anchor: والمراد به النبوة والعلم إلى غير ذلك من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In reality provision belongs only to God; references to other providers or commands to provide are derivative attributions, just as others possess sovereignty and honor only by His gift and permission.
rows.anchor: أن الرزق بحسب الحقيقة لا ينتسب إلا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything creatures receive and benefit from in their existence is their provision from God; many verses on creation, command, judgment, sovereignty, will, governance, and good support this.
rows.anchor: أن ما ينتفع به الخلق في وجودهم مما ينالونه من خير فهو رزقهم والله رازقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God forbids indecency and commands justice, He cannot both forbid an act and command it or restrict His provision to it; forbidden benefit is not provision from the legislative perspective.
rows.anchor: وحاشاه سبحانه أن ينهي عن شيء ثم يأمر به أو ينهي عنه ثم يحصر رزقه فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A forbidden benefit may still be provision from the ontological perspective: creation carries no obligation that would make such a benefit morally blameworthy as a created event.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاة بين عدم كون نفع محرم رزقا بحسب التشريع وكونه رزقا بحسب التكوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān describes provision’s ontological generality without restricting itself to unsophisticated understandings; it is healing for believers and increases wrongdoers only in loss.
rows.anchor: وليس البيان الإلهي بموقوف على الأفهام الساذجة العامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God attributes the dominion of Nimrod and Pharaoh and Qarun’s wealth to His giving as a legislative attribution: permission, trial, completion of proof, abandonment, or gradual enticement.
rows.anchor: فليس إلا أن ذلك كله بإذن الله آتاهم ذلك امتحانا وإتماما للحجة وخذلانا واستدراجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All things are created and sent down from God’s treasuries, and what is with God is good; together these verses show that all a being receives throughout its existence is from God and beneficial to it.
rows.anchor: كل ما يناله شيء في العالم ويتلبس به مدى وجوده فهو من الله سبحانه وهو خير له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān’s statements that God made everything well and is creator of everything reinforce that all created provision is good in itself.
rows.anchor: الذي أحسن كل شيء خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harmfulness of some gifts is relative to their recipient; the same thing may benefit others and serve as good within the causes and order of the universe, as 4:79 indicates.
rows.anchor: فإنما شريته وإضراره نسبي متحقق بالنسبة إلى ما يصيبه خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything God bestows that benefits creation is rizq, since provision means a gift from which its recipient benefits; 20:131 gestures to this meaning.
rows.anchor: إذ ليس الرزق إلا العطية التي ينتفع بها الشيء المرزوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Qurʾānic extension, rizq, good, and creation are equivalent: every provision is good and created, and every created thing is provision and good.
rows.anchor: أن الرزق والخير والخلق بحسب المصداق على ما يبينه القرآن أمور متساوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq presupposes a recipient who needs and uses it; good presupposes a needy seeker choosing what it wants; creation itself requires no prior subject. Food, digestive capacity, and a person illustrate these relations.
rows.anchor: أن الرزق يحتاج إلى فرض مرزوق يرتزق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since all provision and good belong to God, His gifts are given without compensation: everything belongs to Him, and no one has a claim against Him except a right He establishes upon Himself.
rows.anchor: فهو واقع من غير عوض وبلا شيء مأخوذ في مقابله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person who earns through forbidden means has a provision assigned as lawful in the legislative order; God would not make lawful provision due and then provide it unlawfully before punishing the recipient.
rows.anchor: للإنسان المرتزق بالمحرمات رزقا مقدرا من الحلال بنظر التشريع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision parallels mercy: general mercy and provision sustain every creature, while special mercy and provision lead toward felicity and remain within lawful means.
rows.anchor: وكما أن الرحمة رحمتان رحمة عامة تشمل جميع الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As general mercy and provision are decreed, so are special mercy and lawful provision; guidance is legislatively prescribed for every person, believer or unbeliever, through messengers and revealed books.
rows.anchor: كذلك الرحمة الخاصة والرزق الخاص مكتوبان مقدران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawful provision is legislatively decreed, and 6:140 and 16:71 explicitly include both believers and unbelievers, including those who obtain their livelihood lawfully or unlawfully.
rows.anchor: والآيتان كما ترى ذواتا إطلاق قطعي يشمل الكافر والمؤمن ومن يرتزق بالحلال ومن يرتزق بالحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq is what one actually uses: for someone given much wealth who consumes little, only what is eaten is provision in the strict sense; leftover wealth counts only as something bestowed, so provision is not simply wealth’s amount.
rows.anchor: فإنما رزقه هو الذي أكله والزائد الباقي ليس من الرزق إلا من جهة الإيتاء دون الأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Without account” means God’s provision requires no compensation or entitlement from recipients, since all their requests and possessions already belong to Him.
rows.anchor: فلا حساب لرزقه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects interpreting “without account” as unlimited or unmeasured provision: other verses say that every created thing and provision is measured by God.
rows.anchor: وأما كون نفي الحساب راجعا إلى التقدير بمعنى كونه غير محدود ولا مقدر فيدفعه آيات القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion yields four conclusions: all property and sovereignty belong to God; all good is in His hand; provision is His uncompensated gift; and social goods such as wealth, status, and power are provision.
rows.anchor: وقد تحصل من الآيتين أولا أن الملك بضم الميم كله لله كما أن الملك بكسر الميم كله لله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Asked whether God had given the Umayyads sovereignty, al-Ṣādiq answered that God gave it to the Imams and the Umayyads seized it, like someone stealing another man’s garment.
rows.anchor: إن الله عز وجل آتانا الملك وأخذته بني أمية بمنزلة الرجل يكون له الثوب فيأخذه الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives sovereignty ontologically when someone actually exercises power over people, whether justly or unjustly; Nimrod’s rule is an example, and this gives force to commands and decisions.
rows.anchor: إيتاء تكويني وهو انبساط السلطنة على الناس ونفوذ القدرة فيهم سواء كان ذلك بالعدل أو بالظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives sovereignty legislatively by recognizing a ruler whose obedience and authority are owed; this is only just and is a praiseworthy rank, as with Talut.
rows.anchor: وإيتاء تشريعي وهو القضاء بكونه ملكا مفترض الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Umayyads had only actual, ontological rule; the questioner mistakenly attached to it the rightful obedience and religious praise belonging to legislative sovereignty, which the Imam says belongs to the Imams.
rows.anchor: والذي كان لبني أمية من الملك هو المعنى الأول وأثره وقد اشتبه الأمر على راوي الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umayyad rule is blameworthy as usurped and cannot be attributed to God’s granting except as a ruse or gradual enticement, as with Nimrod and Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: فليس إلا مذموما لأنه مغصوب

rows.speaker: يزيد
rows.claim: Yazid claimed that God had awarded his father victory over ʿAlī’s father, acknowledged Fatima’s superiority, and then suggested that al-Ḥusayn may not have read the verse about God’s sovereignty.
rows.anchor: فهذا الذي قتله فأما قوله بأن أبي خير من أب يزيد

rows.speaker: زينب بنت علي
rows.claim: Zaynab rebuked Yazid for treating captivity and apparent worldly success as proof that God honored him; she reminded him that respite for unbelievers increases sin and ends in humiliating punishment.
rows.anchor: أنسيت قول الله { ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا إنما نملي لهم خير لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A reported interpretation takes “bringing the living from the dead and the dead from the living” to mean bringing a believer from an unbeliever and an unbeliever from a believer.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه وتخرج المؤمن من الكافر وتخرج الكافر من المؤمن قال وروي ذلك عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله

rows.speaker: العسكري
rows.claim: Al-Ṣadūq transmits a similar interpretation from al-ʿAskarī concerning the living and dead being brought from one another.
rows.anchor: وروى قريبا منه الصدوق عن العسكري عليه السلام

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: The report says that after creating Adam, God divided his descendants into a right-hand group destined for Paradise and a left-hand group containing the wicked destined for the Fire.
rows.anchor: لما خلق الله آدم عليه السلام أخرج ذريته فقبض قبضة بيمينه

rows.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
rows.claim: A report from Salmān says Adam’s descendants were divided into a right-hand group destined for Paradise and a left-hand group containing the wicked, then mixed; thus believers emerge from unbelievers and unbelievers from believers.
rows.anchor: فخلط بعضهم ببعض فيخرج الكافر من المؤمن ويخرج المؤمن من الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says several exegetical authorities also transmit this meaning from Salmān without a connected chain and classifies the report among traditions about primordial particles and the covenant, to be discussed later.
rows.anchor: والرواية من أخبار الذر والميثاق وسيجيء بيانها في موضع يليق بها إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: In a Farewell Pilgrimage report through Abū Ḥamza from Abū Jaʿfar, the Prophet says no soul dies before completing its provision; one should fear God and seek gracefully, because delayed provision must not tempt sin, and God apportions lawful provision, with unlawful earnings reducing lawful provision and bringing reckoning.
rows.anchor: لا تموت نفس حتى تستكمل رزقها فاتقوا الله وأجملوا في الطلب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī distinguishes provision one seeks from provision that seeks the person; one need not worry about a year ahead, since each day brings its allotted share and no one can take or delay what God decreed.
rows.anchor: الرزق رزقان رزق تطلبه ورزق يطلبك فإن لم تأته أتاك

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report through Jaʿfar from his father says provision descends from heaven in the number of raindrops, allotted to each soul, while God has further bounty that people should ask from Him.
rows.anchor: إن الرزق لينزل من السماء إلى الأرض على عدد قطر المطر إلى كل نفس بما قدر لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Property, understood as exclusive possession, is a necessary human convention whether people live alone or in society.
rows.anchor: أن اعتبار أصل الملك بالكسر من الاعتبارات الضرورية التي لا غنى للبشر عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Political sovereignty is also necessary, chiefly for society: people’s differing aims and wills create conflict over possessions and rights, so a superior power must balance extremes and restore each right.
rows.anchor: لا سبيل إلى رفع هذه الغائلة الطارئة إلا بجعل قوة قاهرة على سائر القوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historically, dominant rulers seized people and property; despite their own injustice, their power sometimes prevented subjects from attacking one another, since rulers kept subjects weak enough not to challenge them.
rows.anchor: وإن كانوا هم أنفسهم وأعضادهم وجلاوزتهم قوى طاغية من غير حق مرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people remained peaceful from fear of rulers, praising their conduct while oppression stayed tolerable and complaining when it exceeded their strength.
rows.anchor: كان يصرف الناس عن الفكر في اعتبار الملك الاجتماعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a ruler died or was killed and disorder threatened, people raised one of the powerful to kingship, after which the old pattern of oppression resumed.
rows.anchor: فبادروا إلى تقديم بعض أولي الطول والقوة منهم وألقوا إليه زمام الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After societies tired of arbitrary royal abuse, they established laws governing government and compelled rulers to follow them, creating limited monarchy that remained hereditary.
rows.anchor: فوضعت قوانين تعين وظائف الحكومة الجارية بين الأمم وأجبرت الملوك باتباعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When inherited monarchy still enabled tyranny, some societies replaced it with public leadership for a fixed term; other political forms arose to escape observed abuses, and future forms may yet emerge.
rows.anchor: فبدلوا الملك برئاسة الجمهور فانقلب الملك المؤبد المشروط إلى ملك مؤجل مشروط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All these reforms show that society needs a position that gathers and directs its competing wills; names and conditions vary, but without a unified will social disorder follows.
rows.anchor: لا غنى للمجتمع الإنساني عن هذا المقام وهو مقام الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kingship is a convention, like other social institutions, that societies keep refining to remove deficiencies and effects opposed to human welfare.
rows.anchor: وهو مثل سائر الموضوعات الاعتبارية التي لم يزل الاجتماع بصدد تكميلها وإصلاحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophethood contributes most to political reform: a widely shared belief that resonates with human instincts and dispositions can unite scattered inclinations into a community acting by one will.
rows.anchor: فإن من المسلم في علم الاجتماع أن انتشار قول ما من الأقوال بين العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From its earliest eras, prophethood called people to justice, forbade oppression, urged worship and submission to God, and rejected Pharaoh-like tyrants; a force repeated across centuries cannot be socially ineffectual.
rows.anchor: ومن المحال أن يلبث مثل هذا العامل القوي بين الاجتماعات الإنسانية قرونا متمادية وهو منعزل عن الأثر خال عن الفعل

rows.speaker: نوح
rows.claim: Noah complains that his people disobeyed him and followed leaders whose wealth and children only increased their loss, while plotting and preserving their idols.
rows.anchor: رب إنهم عصوني واتبعوا من لم يزده ماله وولده إلا خسارا

rows.speaker: نوح
rows.claim: When elites object that only the lowly follow him, Noah says he cannot judge what they did and leaves their reckoning to God.
rows.anchor: قالوا أنؤمن لك واتبعك الأرذلون قال وما علمي بما كانوا يعملون

rows.speaker: هود
rows.claim: Hud condemns his people for building landmarks for amusement, constructing works as though immortal, and striking others with tyrannical force.
rows.anchor: أتبنون بكل ريع آية تعبثون وتتخذون مصانع لعلكم تخلدون

rows.speaker: صالح
rows.claim: Ṣāliḥ tells his people to fear God and obey him, not the extravagant corrupters who do not reform.
rows.anchor: ولا تطيعوا أمر المسرفين الذين يفسدون في الأرض ولا يصلحون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses defended the Israelites against Pharaoh, Abraham opposed Nimrod, and Jesus and other Israelite prophets opposed wealthy rulers and elites, condemning injustice and urging rejection of corrupt authorities.
rows.anchor: وانتهض قبله إبراهيم عليه السلام لمعارضة نمرود ومن بعده عيسى ابن مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān urges resistance to corruption and oppression and warns of the consequences of tyranny; the destruction of ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh is an example.
rows.anchor: فصب عليهم ربك سوط عذاب إن ربك لبالمرصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse following Talut’s story gives the clearest demonstration that sovereignty is necessary for society: without God’s repelling some people by others, the earth would be corrupted.
rows.anchor: أتم بيان قوله تعالى بعد سرد قصة طالوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān contains many verses on sovereignty, authority, and obligatory obedience, while other passages describe kingship as a divine blessing and gift.
rows.anchor: وفي القرآن آيات كثيرة تتعرض للملك والولاية وافتراض الطاعة ونحو ذلك وأخرى تعده نعمة وموهبة
